question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Astute
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Stupid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Astute means clever, shrewd, and quick at noticing and understanding things, especially in order to gain an advantage. (चतुर, बुद्धिमान)
◦ Example: She is an astute businesswoman who never misses a good deal.

• The antonym of astute is a word denoting a lack of intelligence or good judgement — Stupid means lacking intelligence or common sense. (मूर्ख)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Temporary (अस्थायी): lasting for only a limited period of time; not permanent. Unrelated to intelligence.

• Option 3: Illegal (अवैध): not authorised by law; forbidden. Unrelated to intelligence.

• Option 4: Dispute (विवाद): a disagreement or argument. Unrelated to intelligence.

NOTE

• Synonyms of Astute: Shrewd, Sharp, Perceptive, Cunning, Sagacious.

• Other antonym pairs commonly asked: Astute × Naive/Foolish; Shrewd × Gullible.

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the sentences in the correct logical sequence to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
a. This figure is predicted to climb as the percentage of Americans residing in rural areas falls by an average of 1.6% annually.
b. The United Nations reports that India's urban population is growing at a rate of 1.1 percent annually, while the country's rural population is shrinking at a rate of 0.37 percent annually.
c. While 82% of Americans live in urban settings, only 30% of Indians do so.
d. It's still a considerably smaller percentage of the Indian population than it is in the US that resides in urban areas.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. b, d, c, a.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sentence (b) introduces the topic with the UN's statistical report on India's urban and rural population growth rates, making it the ideal opening line.

• Sentence (d) follows logically, drawing a comparison and stating that India's urban population is still smaller in percentage than that of the US.

• Sentence (c) then supplies the specific supporting figures for that comparison — 82% of Americans live in urban areas versus only 30% of Indians.

• Sentence (a) concludes the paragraph, referring back to the 82% figure in (c) ("This figure") and predicting it will rise further as the rural American population keeps shrinking by 1.6% annually.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (d, b, a, c): begins with "d", which uses the comparative phrase "still a considerably smaller percentage... than in the US" without first establishing either country's data — this makes no sense as an opening sentence.

• Option 2 (a, c, b, d): begins with "a", whose opening words "This figure" have no antecedent since no figure has been mentioned yet.

• Option 4 (b, d, a, c): places "a" before "c", but "a" ("This figure is predicted to climb") needs the 82% figure from "c" as its antecedent, so "c" must come before "a".

NOTE

• In para-jumble questions, always locate the sentence that can stand independently as an opening line (introduces the topic without pronouns/demonstratives like "this," "it," "such," referring backward).

• Words like "this," "it," "such," "these" are usually referring/back-linking words — they cannot open a paragraph.

question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
(A) to become severely seasick
(B) a world tour, but he was
(C) a nervous flyer and tended
(D) he wanted to go on
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. DBCA.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correctly arranged sentence reads: "He wanted to go on a world tour, but he was a nervous flyer and tended to become severely seasick."

• Part (D) "he wanted to go on" must open the sentence as it introduces the subject "he" and the main desire being expressed.

• Part (B) "a world tour, but he was" completes the object of "go on" and introduces the contrasting clause with "but".

• Part (C) "a nervous flyer and tended" continues the description of "he was".

• Part (A) "to become severely seasick" completes the infinitive "tended to" logically.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (BADC): would read "a world tour, but he was to become severely seasick a nervous flyer and tended," which is grammatically broken and meaningless.

• Option 2 (ADBC): would read "to become severely seasick a world tour, but he was a nervous flyer and tended," which fails to form a coherent sentence.

• Option 3 (CADB): would read "a nervous flyer and tended to become severely seasick a world tour, but he was," which is illogical and lacks a proper opening subject.

NOTE

• In sentence-rearrangement questions, identify the segment containing the main subject and finite verb first — it is almost always the opening segment.

• Look for connecting words such as "but," "and," "so" to fix the internal order of the remaining segments.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
Study of flying airplanes
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Aviation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Aviation means the designing, building, and flying of aircraft; the study or practice of flying airplanes. (विमानन)
◦ Example: He has always been passionate about aviation and dreams of becoming a pilot.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Alchemy (कीमियागरी): a medieval forerunner of chemistry, concerned with the transmutation of matter, especially attempts to convert base metals into gold.

• Option 3: Astronomy (खगोल विज्ञान): the scientific study of celestial objects such as stars, planets, and galaxies.

• Option 4: Acoustics (ध्वनिविज्ञान): the branch of physics concerned with the properties of sound.

NOTE

• Other one-word substitutions related to fields of study: Ornithology (study of birds), Entomology (study of insects), Cartography (study/making of maps), Numismatics (study of coins).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
A famous company conducted the workshop for its customers.
option_1: The workshop were conducted by a famous company for its customers.
option_2: The workshop had been conducted by a famous company for its customers.
option_3: The workshop was conducted by a famous company for its customers.
option_4: The workshop is conducted by a famous company for its customers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The workshop was conducted by a famous company for its customers.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "A famous company conducted the workshop for its customers" is an assertive sentence in the Simple Past Tense.

• Rule — Simple Past Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + V2 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "the workshop" becomes the subject; being singular it takes "was"; the verb "conducted" becomes the past participle "conducted" (V3); "a famous company" becomes the agent with "by"; and "for its customers" is retained unchanged.
◦ Passive: The workshop was conducted by a famous company for its customers.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "were conducted" wrongly uses the plural auxiliary "were" for the singular subject "the workshop".

• Option 2 is incorrect because "had been conducted" is the passive form of the Past Perfect Tense, not the Simple Past Tense.

• Option 4 is incorrect because "is conducted" is the passive form of the Simple Present Tense, changing the meaning of the original sentence.

NOTE

• In passive voice, the auxiliary verb must always agree in number (singular/plural) and tense with the new subject (the original object).

• Common error: students often confuse "was/were" (Simple Past) with "has/have been" (Present Perfect) or "is/are" (Simple Present) passive forms.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.
How have they been ordered by the minister?
option_1: How have the minister ordered them?
option_2: How had the minister ordered them?
option_3: How did the minister order them?
option_4: How has the minister ordered them?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. How has the minister ordered them?

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "How have they been ordered by the minister?" is an interrogative sentence in the Present Perfect Tense, passive voice.

• Rule — Present Perfect Tense (interrogative):
◦ Passive: Wh-word + has/have + Subject + been + V3 + by + Agent?
◦ Active: Wh-word + has/have + Agent (as new Subject) + V3 + Object?

• Applying the rule: the agent "the minister" (singular) becomes the subject, taking the auxiliary "has"; "been ordered" becomes "ordered" (V3 retained); and "they" becomes the object "them".
◦ Active: How has the minister ordered them?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "have" does not agree with the singular subject "the minister"; it should be "has".

• Option 2 is incorrect because "had ordered" is the active form of the Past Perfect Tense, not the Present Perfect Tense.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "did order" is the active form of the Simple Past Tense, not the Present Perfect Tense.

NOTE

• When converting passive to active, the auxiliary verb (has/have) must match the number of the new subject (the agent introduced by "by").

• "By + agent" in the passive sentence always becomes the subject of the active sentence.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined part of the following sentence.
The playwright has faced many ups and downs in his literary career, which spanned for almost 30 years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. many good and bad times.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "ups and downs" means alternating periods of good luck and bad luck, or successes and failures/misfortunes in life. (अच्छे और बुरे समय)
◦ Example: Every marriage goes through its ups and downs.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "much truth and falsehood" refers to a mix of honesty and lies, which is unrelated to the idiom's meaning.

• Option 2: "many agreements and disagreements" refers to consent and dissent, not to good and bad fortune.

• Option 3: "much light and darkness" is a literal opposite pair and does not capture the figurative sense of fluctuating fortune.

NOTE

• Similar idioms of fluctuating fortune: "A roller-coaster ride," "Swings and roundabouts," "Through thick and thin."

• "Ups and downs" is always used to describe changing circumstances over a period of time, especially in life, career, or relationships.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution’.
The chief guest concluded his speech as he requested to stop by the organisers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. he was requested.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "The chief guest concluded his speech as he requested to stop by the organisers" is grammatically incorrect because the phrase "by the organisers" indicates that the chief guest was the receiver of the request, not the one requesting — so the verb must be in the passive voice.

• Rule — Passive Voice with "by + agent": whenever an action is done "by" someone to the subject, the verb must take the passive form: Subject + was/were + V3 + by + Agent.

• Applying the rule: "he requested" (active) must become "he was requested" (passive), since the organisers are the ones performing the action of requesting, and "he" (the chief guest) receives that request.
◦ Corrected: ...as he was requested to stop by the organisers.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 ("no substitution") is incorrect because the original active form "he requested" contradicts the presence of the agent "by the organisers," making a substitution necessary.

• Option 3 ("he is requested") is incorrect because it uses the Simple Present Tense, which does not match the Simple Past Tense of the main verb "concluded".

• Option 4 ("he will be requested") is incorrect because it uses the Future Tense, which is inconsistent with the past narration of the sentence.

NOTE

• Whenever a sentence contains "by + someone" acting upon the subject, check whether the verb should be passive rather than active.

• The tense of the passive verb must always match the tense of the rest of the sentence.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
He was / bad injured / in the / last match.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. bad injured.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The segment "bad injured" is grammatically incorrect because "injured" here describes the manner/extent of harm, and it must be modified by an adverb, not an adjective.

• Rule — Adjective vs Adverb: An adjective (e.g., "bad") modifies a noun or pronoun, while an adverb (e.g., "badly") modifies a verb, adjective, or another adverb, describing how an action is done.

• Since "injured" is being described in terms of degree/manner, it needs the adverb "badly," not the adjective "bad".
◦ Corrected: He was badly injured in the last match.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 ("last match.") is grammatically correct as it stands and needs no change.

• Option 2 ("in the") is a correct prepositional phrase and needs no change.

• Option 4 ("He was") is a grammatically correct subject-verb combination and needs no change.

NOTE

• Common adjective/adverb confusion pairs tested in SSC exams: bad/badly, good/well, quick/quickly, careful/carefully.

• Remember: adverbs of manner typically end in "-ly" and answer the question "how?"

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in brackets to fill in the blank.
She __________ requested him to pay the bills. (persistently)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. continuously.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Persistently means continuing firmly or obstinately in a course of action in spite of difficulty or opposition; happening repeatedly over a period of time. (लगातार, दृढ़ता से)
◦ Example: She persistently reminded him about the pending payment.

• Among the given options, "continuously" (लगातार, बिना रुके) is the closest in meaning, denoting an action that keeps happening again and again without stopping.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Impetuously (उतावलेपन से) means acting quickly and without thought; impulsively — this conveys suddenness, not repeated persistence.

• Option 2: Obliviously (अनजाने में) means in a manner showing no awareness of something; unmindfully — this is unrelated to persistence.

• Option 3: Tremendously (अत्यधिक) means to a great extent; extremely — this describes intensity, not the repeated/continuing nature of an action.

NOTE

• Persistently is close in meaning to: continuously, repeatedly, doggedly, relentlessly, insistently.

• Do not confuse "persistently" (repeated effort/continuation) with "impetuously" (hasty, without thought), which is nearly opposite in connotation.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Coy
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Extroverted.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Coy means (especially of a woman) making a pretence of shyness or modesty that is intended to be alluring; reluctant to give details about something, reticent. (शर्मीला, संकोची)
◦ Example: She gave a coy smile when asked about her new relationship.

• The antonym of coy is a word describing outgoing, bold, and socially confident behaviour — Extroverted means outgoing, socially confident, and comfortable interacting with others. (बहिर्मुखी)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Shy (शर्मीला) is a synonym of coy, not its antonym.

• Option 2: Uptight (तनावग्रस्त) means nervous, anxious, or unable to relax — this is not the opposite of coy either.

• Option 3: Recent (हाल का) means happening or done a short time ago — unrelated to shyness.

NOTE

• Synonyms of Coy: Bashful, Demure, Reticent, Shy.

• Antonyms of Coy: Extroverted, Bold, Brazen, Confident, Outgoing.

question:
Complete the sentence with the most appropriate set of ANTONYMS of the highlighted word.
‘Grisly’.
The other day Jimmy behaved _______ with Jammy and that was quite _______ for me.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. pleasantly, comforting.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Grisly means causing horror or disgust; gruesome, ghastly. (भयानक, डरावना)
◦ Example: The news report described the grisly details of the accident.

• Since the question asks for the antonyms of "Grisly" to complete the sentence, the blanks should be filled with words meaning pleasant and comforting, which are opposite in sense to something gruesome or horrifying.
◦ Completed: The other day Jimmy behaved pleasantly with Jammy and that was quite comforting for me.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "rudely, attractive" — "rudely" (behaving impolitely) is not an antonym of grisly, and mixing it with "attractive" creates an inconsistent pair.

• Option 2: "disgusting, atrocious" — both words are synonyms of grisly (gruesome/horrifying), not antonyms.

• Option 3: "ghastly, shameless" — "ghastly" is itself a synonym of grisly, and "shameless" is unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of Grisly: Gruesome, Ghastly, Horrific, Macabre, Grim.

• Antonyms of Grisly: Pleasant, Delightful, Comforting, Agreeable.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Customary
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Unusual.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Customary means according to the customs or usual practices associated with a particular society, place, or set of circumstances; habitual, usual. (प्रथागत, रिवाजी)
◦ Example: It is customary to remove your shoes before entering a temple.

• The antonym of customary is a word meaning not habitual or not usually done — Unusual means not habitually or commonly occurring; out of the ordinary. (असामान्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Fashion (फैशन) means a popular trend, especially in clothing — not an antonym of customary.

• Option 2: Protection (सुरक्षा) means the act of keeping someone/something safe — unrelated to customary.

• Option 3: Habitual (आदतन) is actually a synonym of customary (both mean "usual" or "habitual"), not its antonym — this option is a common distractor.

NOTE

• Synonyms of Customary: Habitual, Usual, Traditional, Conventional, Routine.

• Antonyms of Customary: Unusual, Uncommon, Exceptional, Rare.

question:
Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank.
The _____ of the flowers spread everywhere when they bloom.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. scent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Scent means a distinctive smell, especially one that is pleasant; a fragrance, particularly of flowers. The sentence requires this word since it refers to the fragrance of flowers spreading.
◦ Example: The scent of jasmine filled the entire garden.

• Rule — Homophones: Homophones are words that sound alike but have different meanings and spellings. "Sent," "saint," "scent," and "cent" all sound similar but differ completely in meaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "sent" is the past tense/past participle of "send," meaning to cause something to go or be taken to a destination.

• Option 2: "saint" refers to a holy or virtuous person, especially one formally recognised by a Christian Church.

• Option 4: "cent" refers to a monetary unit equal to one-hundredth of a dollar or similar currency.

NOTE

• Other commonly confused homophone sets in SSC exams: "principal/principle," "stationary/stationery," "counsel/council," "peace/piece," "flour/flower."

• Always determine the meaning required by the context of the sentence before selecting the correct homophone.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
My sister and I / work very hard / nevertheless my brother does not do / any task assigned to him.
option_1: nevertheless my brother does not do
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. nevertheless my brother does not do.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "My sister and I work very hard nevertheless my brother does not do any task assigned to him" incorrectly uses "nevertheless" to join two contrasting clauses within a single sentence.

• Rule — Nevertheless vs Whereas: "Nevertheless" is a conjunctive adverb meaning "in spite of that; notwithstanding" and is generally used to begin a new independent sentence or clause after a semicolon/full stop, not to directly connect two contrasting subjects within one sentence. To directly contrast two different subjects' actions within a single sentence, a subordinating conjunction like "whereas" or "while" is required.

• Applying the rule, "nevertheless" should be replaced with "whereas" to correctly show the contrast between the hardworking sister/narrator and the brother who avoids work.
◦ Corrected: My sister and I work very hard, whereas my brother does not do any task assigned to him.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 ("work very hard") is grammatically correct and needs no change.

• Option 3 ("any task assigned to him.") is grammatically correct and needs no change.

• Option 4 ("My sister and I") is a grammatically correct compound subject and needs no change.

NOTE

• "Whereas" and "while" are used to contrast two facts within the same sentence.

• "Nevertheless" and "however" are conjunctive adverbs used to introduce a contrasting idea, typically as a new sentence or after a semicolon, not as a direct joining word between two clauses of one sentence.

question:
Select the correct meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence.
Lucy's conceited conduct with her colleagues has left her high and dry
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Helpless.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "left high and dry" means left without help, in a difficult situation, stranded, or abandoned without the resources or support one needs. (असहाय छोड़ देना)
◦ Example: When the company shut down overnight, the employees were left high and dry.

• The idiom originates from a ship that has run aground and is stranded on dry land, out of the water, unable to move — hence the imagery of being stuck and helpless.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Superseding (अधिक्रमण करना) means taking the place of, especially in terms of power, authority, or use — unrelated to the idiom's meaning.

• Option 3: Impoverished (गरीब) means made poor; reduced to poverty — this is not what "high and dry" means.

• Option 4: "Surrounded by people" is the literal opposite of being stranded/abandoned, and is not related to the idiom's meaning at all.

NOTE

• Other idioms meaning "helpless/abandoned": "Left in the lurch," "Left out in the cold," "Left holding the baby."

• Do not confuse "high and dry" (helpless/stranded) with "high and mighty" (arrogant, self-important).

question: Select the correct spelling of the word that means ‘to replace’.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Supersede.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Supersede," meaning to take the place of (a person or thing previously in authority or use); to replace, especially with something newer or superior.
◦ Example: The new safety regulations will supersede the old ones from next month.

• Spelling key: SUPER + SEDE. This is one of only a few English words ending in "-sede" (not "-ceed" or "-cede"); it comes from Latin "supersedere," meaning "to sit above."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Superceed" is incorrect; there is no such ending as "-ceed" combined with "super-".

• Option 2: "Supersed" is incorrect; it is missing the final "e".

• Option 3: "Superseed" is incorrect; the ending "-seed" is wrong — it should be "-sede".

NOTE

• Only one common English word ends in "-sede": Supersede. Three words end in "-ceed": Exceed, Proceed, Succeed. All other similar words end in "-cede": Precede, Recede, Concede, Intercede, Secede.

• This "-cede/-ceed/-sede" distinction is a frequently tested SSC spelling trap.

question:
Select the word segment that can substitute the bracketed word segment correctly and complete the sentence meaningfully.
We will have to (put the meeting away) as the Director is not well.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. put the meeting off.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "put off" means to postpone or delay an event to a later time. (स्थगित करना)
◦ Example: Due to heavy rain, they had to put the picnic off till next weekend.

• Since the Director is unwell, the meeting logically needs to be postponed/delayed, not moved in some other way — "put the meeting off" correctly and meaningfully conveys this.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "put the meeting up" — "put up" means to erect, build, or provide accommodation; it makes no sense in the context of a meeting and the Director's illness.

• Option 3: "put the meeting on" — "put on" means to stage, present, or wear something; it does not convey postponement.

• Option 4: "put the meeting again" is grammatically incomplete/incorrect; "put again" is not a standard phrasal verb combination.

NOTE

• Other common phrasal verbs with "put": put up with (tolerate), put across (communicate clearly), put down (write down/humiliate), put forward (propose), put away (store).

• "Put off" (postpone) should not be confused with "put out" (extinguish) or "put up with" (tolerate).

question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
(a) one of the primary obstacles encountered
(b) is the risk of sample contamination
(c) during the analysis of controlled dangerous substance (CDS)
(d) from improper handling and collecting methodologies
(e) proof bloodstain patterns and DNA evidence
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. acebd.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correctly arranged sentence reads: "One of the primary obstacles encountered during the analysis of controlled dangerous substance (CDS), proof bloodstain patterns and DNA evidence, is the risk of sample contamination from improper handling and collecting methodologies."

• Part (a) "one of the primary obstacles encountered" must open the sentence, introducing the main subject of discussion.

• Part (c) "during the analysis of controlled dangerous substance (CDS)" specifies where/when this obstacle is encountered, directly following (a).

• Part (e) "proof bloodstain patterns and DNA evidence" lists the additional types of forensic evidence analysed alongside CDS.

• Part (b) "is the risk of sample contamination" supplies the main verb and complement, naming the obstacle itself.

• Part (d) "from improper handling and collecting methodologies" completes the sentence by explaining the cause of the contamination risk.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (eacdb): begins with "e" ("proof bloodstain patterns and DNA evidence"), which cannot logically open the sentence without first stating "one of the primary obstacles encountered".

• Option 3 (aecdb): places "e" immediately after "a" and before "c", breaking the logical link between "obstacles encountered" and "during the analysis of CDS", and ends awkwardly on "is the risk of sample contamination" without its cause.

• Option 4 (abcde): places "b" ("is the risk of sample contamination") too early, and ends the sentence on "e" ("proof bloodstain patterns and DNA evidence"), which trails off without completing the thought about contamination's cause.

NOTE

• In complex sentence-rearrangement questions, first identify the main subject-verb pair (here, "one of the primary obstacles... is the risk...") and then fit the remaining descriptive/prepositional phrases around it in a logical sequence.

• Phrases beginning with prepositions like "during," "from," "with" usually function as modifiers and should be placed immediately after the noun/clause they describe.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Convinient.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Convinient" is the incorrectly spelt word; the correct spelling is "Convenient," meaning fitting in well with a person's needs, activities, and plans; suitable or opportune.
◦ Example: Please let me know a convenient time for the meeting.

• Spelling key: CON + VEN + IENT. Note the "e" in the second syllable "ven," not "vin" — the word derives from Latin "convenire," meaning "to come together, agree, be suitable".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Embarrass" is spelt correctly — meaning to cause someone to feel awkward, self-conscious, or ashamed. (Note the double "r" and double "s".)

• Option 3: "National" is spelt correctly — meaning relating to or belonging to a nation.

• Option 4: "Discipline" is spelt correctly — meaning the practice of training people to obey rules, or controlled behaviour.

NOTE

• Commonly misspelt words related to this one: "Convenience" (not "Convinience"), "Convenor" (not "Convinor").

• Always watch for the vowel substituted incorrectly (i for e) in words like Convenient, Definite, Separate — frequent SSC spelling traps.

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Global warming is a major problem. The result will be the problems created by the rising temperatures of the Arctic region. As a result of global warming, (1)_________ in rainfall and plant distribution affect the migration patterns, feeding behaviour, and breeding preferences of numerous bird species. The increase in the temperature may also alter ocean currents, which may alter the (2)_________ ecology as a whole. Greenhouse gas emissions are responsible for the ongoing melting of the Arctic. This will result in a (3)_________ loop since greenhouse gases trap the heat in the atmosphere and the additional emissions may (4)_________ the global warming process. Now, the only way to reverse the harm is for every person to be environmentally sensitive. This may offer us hope that we will be able to leave a green planet to our future generations, who presently appear to face (5)_________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. alterations.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a noun describing a change in rainfall and plant distribution that goes on to affect birds' migration, feeding, and breeding patterns.

• "Alterations" means changes or modifications, which fits perfectly with the cause-and-effect relationship described — changes in rainfall and plant distribution affecting bird behaviour.
◦ Completed: As a result of global warming, alterations in rainfall and plant distribution affect the migration patterns...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "stabilisation" means the process of becoming stable/steady — this contradicts the passage's theme of harmful, ongoing environmental change caused by global warming.

• Option 2: "stagnation" means a state of not developing, growing, or being active — this does not fit the idea of shifting rainfall/plant patterns.

• Option 3: "fixation" means an obsessive interest in something, or the act of fixing something in place — neither meaning fits the context of changing rainfall patterns.

NOTE

• In cloze passages, always read the whole sentence (and often the surrounding sentences) to identify whether the blank requires a word suggesting change, growth, decline, or stability, based on the passage's overall tone.

• The overall tone of this passage is about global warming causing continuous negative environmental change, so words implying "change" (like alterations) fit better than words implying stability.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. marine.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank follows a sentence about rising temperature altering "ocean currents," so the ecology being affected must logically be connected to the ocean.

• "Marine" means relating to the sea, especially with reference to seaborne trade, navigation, or ecology — hence "marine ecology" (ocean-related ecosystem) is the most contextually appropriate fit.
◦ Completed: ...may also alter ocean currents, which may alter the marine ecology as a whole.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "grassland" refers to land ecosystems covered with grass, unrelated to ocean currents.

• Option 2: "biosphere" refers to the entire global ecological system, which is too broad and non-specific given that the sentence is specifically about ocean currents.

• Option 4: "landscape" refers to the visible features of an area of land, which is unrelated to the ocean context of the sentence.

NOTE

• Always match the blank word to the specific noun/topic mentioned just before it in the sentence — here, "ocean currents" directly signals that a sea/ocean-related word ("marine") is required.

• Related word: "Marine ecosystem" is a standard collocation frequently used in environment-related passages.

This may offer us hope that we will be able to leave a green planet to our future generations, who presently appear to face (5)_________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. vicious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank describes a type of "loop" in which greenhouse gases trap heat and that trapped heat, in turn, worsens the greenhouse effect — a self-reinforcing, harmful cycle.

• "Vicious" combined with "loop/circle/cycle" forms the fixed collocation "vicious cycle/loop" — a sequence of events in which each event seems to reinforce or intensify the one before it, typically to a negative or harmful effect.
◦ Completed: This will result in a vicious loop since greenhouse gases trap the heat...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "feeble" means lacking physical strength or power; weak — this does not collocate meaningfully with "loop" in this context.

• Option 2: "gentle" means mild or moderate in action, effect, or degree — this contradicts the passage's description of a worsening, harmful process.

• Option 4: "moderate" means average in amount, intensity, or degree — this also contradicts the idea of an intensifying, harmful cycle.

NOTE

• "Vicious cycle/circle/loop" is a very commonly tested fixed collocation in SSC exams, meaning a harmful, self-perpetuating chain of cause and effect.

• Its opposite collocation is "virtuous cycle," describing a favourable, self-reinforcing chain of events.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. accelerate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a verb describing what the "additional emissions" do to the "global warming process," in a sentence already describing a worsening, self-reinforcing (vicious) loop.

• "Accelerate" means to cause something to happen sooner, faster, or more quickly; to speed up — this logically fits since more greenhouse gas emissions would speed up/worsen global warming.
◦ Completed: ...the additional emissions may accelerate the global warming process.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "hinder" means to create difficulty for someone, resulting in delay or obstruction — this is the opposite of what additional emissions would do to global warming.

• Option 2: "repress" means to restrain or prevent an emotion or natural tendency from being expressed — it does not fit a physical/environmental process like global warming.

• Option 3: "restrain" means to keep under control or restrict — again the opposite effect from what more emissions would actually cause.

NOTE

• Since the passage has already described a "vicious loop," the logical continuation must be a word meaning "worsen/speed up," not "slow down/control" — always check consistency of tone across the whole passage.

• Synonyms of accelerate: hasten, expedite, quicken, speed up. Antonyms: hinder, restrain, decelerate, impede.

solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. extinction.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank describes what "future generations" presently "appear to face" as a consequence of unchecked global warming — the passage's overall tone is a warning about severe, harmful environmental consequences.

• "Extinction" means the state or process of a species, family, or larger group being or becoming extinct — in a broader sense here, it conveys the severe threat of species/life being wiped out due to environmental damage, matching the passage's cautionary tone.
◦ Completed: ...future generations, who presently appear to face extinction.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "renovation" means the process of improving or repairing something, especially a building — this has a positive connotation unrelated to a dire warning about the future.

• Option 3: "redemption" means the action of saving someone from sin, error, or evil; deliverance — this is also a positive outcome, contradicting the passage's warning tone.

• Option 4: "salvation" means preservation or deliverance from harm or difficulty — again a positive outcome, the opposite of the negative consequence the passage is warning about.

NOTE

• The passage consistently uses a cautionary/alarming tone about the harmful effects of global warming, so the final blank must continue this negative tone rather than switch to a positive resolution.

• "Extinction" is commonly used in environmental passages regarding the loss of biodiversity and species due to climate change.
